label: Signed state code: + at S1 and - at S2 at D2; at D1, high after S2 or no reward.
terms: (phase == D2) * (3 - 2 * state) ;; (phase == D1) * (in_rew == 1) * (prev_state == S1) ;; (phase == D1) * (in_rew == 1) * (prev_state == S2) ;; (phase == D1) * (in_rew == 0) * (prev_state == S1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == S2) ;; (phase == D1) * (ep_trial == 0)
explanation: The raw candidate value n of unit 31 mostly encodes the state the agent sees. At D2 it is about +0.85 when S1 is shown and -0.85 when S2 is shown, and this one term carries most of the variance. At the next D1 the sign flips relative to the last state: the value is high (about +0.7) after reaching S2 or after no reward, and low or negative after a rewarded trial, most negative after S1 rewarded. GO stays near its baseline with little history dependence. The free fit adds the reward x state interaction at D1, a D1 offset for a2 choices, small GO terms and a first-trial offset, but it only gains about 0.005 R^2 over the short form. Belief log-odds adds nothing once state and reward are in. No future variables are used.

issues: The short form holds up. It gets test R^2 0.898 beyond timing, against a 0.96 ceiling. The D2 state term alone gives 0.744, so it does most of the work. The two D1 terms each pull their weight: swapping prev_state==S2 for prev_action==2 drops it to 0.868, and using belief_lo at D1 in place of the state term drops it to 0.836.

The label's 'at D1, high after S2 or no reward' reads as an OR, which overstates things. The fit is additive: in_rew==1 has weight -0.44 and prev_state==S2 has weight +0.56. The profile residuals at D1 are: a1 S1 u -0.05, a2 S1 u +0.24, a1 S2 r -0.16, a2 S2 r +0.21, S2 u +0.43/+0.67, S1 r -0.60/-0.36. So no reward after S1 does not make it high (a1 S1 u is about baseline), and S2 with reward is only middling. A better wording is 'raised after reaching S2, lowered after reward'. An interaction form (rewarded at S1 low, unrewarded at S2 high) scores the same, 0.8999 test.

The misses show no large systematic errors. Mean error by phase is at most 0.03. The largest cells are D1 after a1 S2 r (-0.31, over-predicted) and GO after the previous reward (about +0.2 when rewarded, -0.25 when not), which matches the free fit's small GO terms. The 'D1 after ?' under-prediction (+0.26) comes from the first trial in a window, where prev_state is unknown, so it is a data artifact.
The D2 magnitude claim checks out: the residual is +0.85/+0.75 at S1 and -0.69/-0.78 at S2. No future variables are used.
